cells.note: Outline is structural (no card halo); F2 reinterpreted as fold/collapse + focus activate/move/expand. Collapse vs jump axis purity holds (chevron onClick stopPropagation, OutlinePanel.tsx:638-641,959). Focus-edit row click routes to onFocusMoveTo/onFocusExpandTo not onScrollTo (:617-625) — clean. BUT focus activate/move/expand reads outlineHeadings derived from latestDoc which is NULL until the first doc edit (EditorLayout.tsx:1094,2360-2362; latestDoc only set by 300ms-debounced handleUpdate which fires on doc CHANGE, never on create — Editor.tsx:796) → on a pristine doc Focus targets the whole doc, not the first section. See OUT-F2-01.

Card→text jump (row click → onScrollTo(blockIndex) → handleScrollToHeading → scrollToHeading) is index-consistent: both the outline rows and scrollToHeading walk the LIVE editor doc, so indices align even with duplicate heading names (keyed by block index, OutlinePanel.tsx:322; Editor.tsx:944-958). Reverse (text→outline) position lozenge matches data-outline-pos live (OutlinePanel.tsx:631,1268). Defects: (a) focus-band bottom-handle snap onto a parTitle row expands to the WHOLE enclosing section while the top-handle snaps to the exact paragraph — asymmetric (OUT-F3-01); (b) split-pane bottom-pane docstart/heading jump moves the MAIN editor's text selection as a side effect (OUT-F3-02); (c) outline row LABEL can be stale after an in-place heading rename so the row a user clicks shows old text though the jump target is correct (see OUT-F7-01).

Outline is a structural panel with no cards; there is no card kind to morph (panel-registry/no card-registry entry; OutlinePanel.tsx renders headings/parTitles, not EditableCard). Morph (report↔report-request etc.) does not apply. Brief S6 lists F6 as N/A.

No delete/duplicate affordance (structural panel). Lifecycle here = drag-reorder (edit mode) + inline rename. Drag-reorder mechanics are sound (slice/delete/insert with self-range guard, OutlinePanel.tsx:1089 + editor-ops.ts:88-119; the observer emits changedBlocks+blockOrderChanged for the single-tx move so footnote/citation renumber is preserved per step-inspector.test.ts:81-102). Defects: (a) after a successful heading or parTitle rename via the edit-mode pod, the outline keeps showing the OLD title because an in-place text/attr edit fires no structural bus event → no rev.* bump → EditorPane does not re-render → content (editor.getJSON()) stays stale (OUT-F7-01); (b) the outline's OWN drag-reorder shifts block indices, corrupting the index-keyed persisted collapse Set — same root as the sibling A2 finding (OUT-outline-g-anchor OUT-A2-01); cross-referenced, not re-claimed. Heading-rename atom DATA-LOSS is claimed by g-display (OUT-F5-01); parTitle setNodeMarkup type-guard gap by g-anchor (OUT-F8-04).

findings.subject: outline
findings.symptom: On a freshly-opened document that has not been edited yet, clicking the outline 'Focus' button focuses the ENTIRE document instead of the first section, and (once in focus-edit mode) clicking any section row focuses the whole document rather than that section.
findings.suspectedRootCause: The focus-mode action handlers are fed `outlineHeadings`/`outlineTotalBlocks` derived exclusively from `latestDoc` (EditorLayout.tsx:2360-2362, `const docForOutline = latestDoc`). `latestDoc` starts `null` (EditorLayout.tsx:1094) and is only ever assigned inside the 300ms-debounced `handleUpdate` (editor-ops.ts:39-51), which is wired to TipTap's `onUpdate` (Editor.tsx:796) — `onUpdate` fires on a doc CHANGE, never on editor create. So until the user makes their first edit, `outlineHeadings === []` and `outlineTotalBlocks === 0`. `useFocusActions` threads that empty list into `focusMode.activate`/`moveTo`/`expandTo` (focus.ts:21-38); with `headings.length === 0`, `activate` takes its `start=0,end=totalBlocks-1` branch = `[0,-1]` (useFocusMode.ts:264-268) and `sectionRange` returns `[0, totalBlocks-1]` for moveTo (useFocusMode.ts:144) → `bandFromIndices(doc,0,-1)` resolves to `{startUuid:null,endUuid:null}` = whole-doc band (useFocusMode.ts:99-113). Meanwhile the OUTLINE itself renders fine because its `content` prop is the LIVE `editor.getJSON()` (EditorPane.tsx:3400/3473), so the user sees real sections but the focus engine sees none. This is the empty/null-snapshot endpoint of the same debounced-vs-live divergence the sibling g-anchor finding OUT-F8-02 reports for the 300ms post-edit window; the pristine-doc case is both more common (every doc open) and more severe (band is empty, not merely off-by-a-section).

evidence.note: docForOutline = latestDoc; outlineHeadings/outlineTotalBlocks derived from it (2361-2362)
setLatestDoc fired only inside the 300ms debounce timer; never seeded on editor ready
onUpdate handler — fires on doc change only, not on create, so latestDoc stays null on a never-edited doc
activate: headings.length===0 → start=0,end=totalBlocks-1 (=-1 when totalBlocks 0) → whole-doc band

reproSteps: Open a document containing several headings and do NOT type anything.
Observe: the whole document is 'focused' (no section is dimmed) instead of the first section being isolated.
Alternatively, enter focus-edit mode (Focus on) on a pristine doc and click section 3's row → the band still covers the whole doc rather than section 3.
Now type one character anywhere, wait ~300ms, repeat: Focus now correctly isolates the first section.
findings.suspectedClass: Any consumer that derives structure from the debounced `latestDoc` instead of the live editor while the user can interact before the first edit. Sibling: `availableDividerLevels`/`activeDividerLevels` (EditorLayout.tsx:2363-2374) is also empty until the first edit, so the toolbar's divider-level menu is empty on a pristine doc; `focusWordCount` (EditorLayout.tsx:2387-2392) likewise reads `docForOutline`. The deeper class is the live-vs-debounced snapshot split flagged in g-anchor OUT-F8-02.

findings.subject: outline
findings.symptom: After renaming a heading or a paragraph-title from the outline's edit-mode pod, the outline keeps displaying the OLD title; the rename did land in the document but the panel does not reflect it until some unrelated structural edit (e.g. adding/removing a block) forces a refresh.
findings.suspectedRootCause: The outline's `content` prop is `editor.getJSON()` evaluated during EditorPane render (EditorPane.tsx:3400/3473), and EditorPane only re-renders when a `useStructuralRevisions` counter bumps (it consumes `rev` whose object identity changes on any counter bump — useStructuralRevisions.ts:79-91). Heading-text rename goes through `handleRenameHeading` = `tr.delete(from,to).insertText(newText, from)` strictly INSIDE the heading node (editor-ops.ts:123-138); this is an in-place ReplaceStep that neither adds/removes the heading block nor changes a structural attr, so the step inspector emits no heading event (headingStructurallyChanged compares only level/label/numbered — step-inspector.ts:247; text-only changes don't surface in changedHeadings — :622-623) → `rev.headings` does not bump → EditorPane does not re-render → `editor.getJSON()` is not recomputed → the OutlineNode/EditablePod text (read from `content`) stays stale. ParTitle rename is worse: `handleRenameParTitle` does `setNodeMarkup(offset, undefined, {...attrs, parTitle})` (editor-ops.ts:160-174); the step inspector synthesizes added/removed entries ONLY for heading level/label/numbered and figureBlock label/numbered (step-inspector.ts:483-528), NOT for a paragraph's `parTitle` attr, so no counter bumps at all. By contrast a heading LABEL edit DOES refresh (it bumps rev.headings via the synthesized entries at :486-507), which is exactly why the discrepancy is easy to miss. Net: the propose→apply round-trip for the two rename operations the outline edit-mode pod exposes is not reflected back into the panel.

evidence.note: handleRenameHeading: in-place delete+insertText inside the heading node — no block add/remove, no attr change
handleRenameParTitle: setNodeMarkup parTitle attr — not tracked by the step inspector
headingStructurallyChanged compares level/label/numbered only — heading text edits never produce changedHeadings
attr-step synthesis only for heading level/label/numbered and figureBlock — paragraph parTitle attr not handled
outline content = editor.getJSON() at render time; only refreshed when EditorPane re-renders
rev counters bump only on bus events; a structurally-null edit fires none, so no re-render

reproSteps: Open the outline panel and click 'Edit' to enter edit mode.
Click a heading pod's text, change the title (e.g. 'Intro' → 'Introduction'), press Enter.
Observe the document heading updates but the outline pod still reads 'Intro'.
Repeat with a paragraph-title pod — same staleness.
Add or delete any block to force a structural re-render → the outline now shows the new titles.
Contrast: editing a heading's label refreshes the outline immediately (label is a tracked structural attr).
findings.suspectedClass: Any outline/derived-view value sourced from `editor.getJSON()` that must reflect an in-place text or untracked-attr edit: the outline heading row text also fails to live-update while a user types a heading title directly in the main editor (same no-rev-bump path), and the per-section word count + section-number columns ride the same `content` snapshot. The deeper class is 'in-place content edits that no structural counter observes, consumed by a memoized/gated render.' Live verification would confirm whether any incidental EditorPane re-render (selectionUpdate subscriber, etc.) masks this in practice.

findings.subject: outline
findings.symptom: Dragging the focus-band BOTTOM handle and releasing it on a paragraph-title (parTitle) row extends the band to the end of that paragraph's entire enclosing section, whereas dragging the TOP handle onto a parTitle row snaps the band start to that exact paragraph — the two handles treat the same row type inconsistently.
findings.suspectedRootCause: FocusBand's drag candidate set (`allRowAttrs`) includes parTitle rows as snap targets (OutlinePanel.tsx:1236-1249), and onSnapBoundary is called with the raw block index of the snapped row (:1326). In `focusMode.snapBoundary` the TOP edge uses the index directly as the new start (`bandFromIndices(doc, blockIndex, cur.endIdx, ...)`, useFocusMode.ts:363-366), but the BOTTOM edge passes the index through `sectionRange(blockIndex, headings, totalBlocks)` and uses `newEnd` (useFocusMode.ts:367-369). When `blockIndex` is a parTitle (a paragraph, not a heading), `sectionRange` finds no matching heading (findIndex === -1) and falls through to the enclosing-heading branch, returning that heading's WHOLE [start,end] range (useFocusMode.ts:133-153) — so the bottom edge jumps to the section end rather than to the dropped paragraph. The asymmetry is structural: top treats the row as a literal boundary, bottom treats it as 'the section this row belongs to'.

evidence.note: allRowAttrs includes h.parTitles as draggable snap candidates
snapBoundary top edge: uses blockIndex directly as start
snapBoundary bottom edge: routes blockIndex through sectionRange → whole-section end for a parTitle
sectionRange returns the enclosing heading's full range when blockIndex is not itself a heading

reproSteps: Enable 'Show par. titles' and activate (unlocked) Focus mode on a section that contains several titled paragraphs.
Drag the band's TOP handle down onto the row of the 2nd titled paragraph — the band start snaps to exactly that paragraph.
Drag the band's BOTTOM handle up onto the row of a titled paragraph mid-section — the band end snaps to the END of the whole enclosing section, not to that paragraph.
Observe the two handles do not behave symmetrically for the same kind of target row.
findings.suspectedClass: Boundary operations that route one edge through section-rounding (`sectionRange`) and the other through a raw index. `nudgeBoundary` (useFocusMode.ts:318-349, currently UNWIRED) repeats the same top=raw / bottom=sectionRange split, so if keyboard nudge is ever wired it inherits the asymmetry.

findings.subject: outline
findings.symptom: In split-pane mode with the bottom pane active, clicking an outline heading (or the 'Document start' row) to navigate the bottom pane also silently moves the MAIN (top) editor's text cursor.
findings.suspectedRootCause: `handleScrollToHeading`, when routing a jump to the mirror (bottom) pane, calls `editor.commands.setTextSelection(...)` on the canonical MAIN editor and then scrolls the MIRROR view's DOM (editor-ops.ts:56-81). Because the mirror is a second EditorView over the same shared state, setting the selection moves the single shared selection — felt as the top pane's cursor jumping even though the user only intended to navigate the bottom pane. The docstart branch is the same: `editor.commands.setTextSelection(1)` then scrolls the mirror scroll container (editor-ops.ts:59-63).

evidence.note: split bottom-pane docstart: setTextSelection(1) on the main editor, then scroll mirror
split bottom-pane heading jump: setTextSelection(pos) on the main editor (shared selection) before scrolling mirror

reproSteps: Open split-pane view; click into the bottom pane to make it active.
Click a heading in the outline.
Observe the bottom pane scrolls to the heading AND the top pane's text cursor relocates to that heading position.
findings.suspectedClass: Jump handlers that set the shared editor selection as a means of scrolling a secondary view. Any panel jump routed to the mirror via the same setTextSelection-on-shared-state pattern would perturb the main pane's caret.
